comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: CAMPAIGN STATE (2026-09-18T20:2x UTC). Universe 40 plans x 6 arms = 240 cells, 720 observations at n=3. Credited 316, owed 404, void 20. Cells at n=3: 62. Plans complete across all six arms: 9 (2127-348c-BLOCK, 2127-348c-PASS, 2948-48e5-BLOCK, 2948-48e5-PASS, 36ab-b649-PASS, 5200-e04e-PASS, 86ac-086a-PASS, d23e-1012-BLOCK, eb6e-f43a-PASS). Cohort 1 is ready=True, owed 0 -- the first fully complete judging cohort. Owed by arm: gstack 88, mini 81, rebar 60, ce 59, sp 58, sp5 58. Six supervisor lanes dispatching (cohort02-05 plus two earlier). Arms and backends: rebar -> Bedrock opus-4-8 finders; mini -> its own API path on sonnet-4-6; ce/sp/sp5/gstack -> claude -p.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: OPERATOR DECISIONS RECORDED. (a) mini step-limit flag moved out of JUDGE_BLOCKING_FLAGS, which is now ('poolability_unresolved',) alone -- mini reaching its 260-step ceiling is a property of the tool under test, travels as advisory. (b) ce_spawn_depth set to 'pool' and persisted in campaign_plan.json; CE's canonical reviews pool with runner-produced replicates. (c) rebar description ceiling raised 120000 -> 160000 in harness/rebar-bakeoff.toml (rebar ships 8000; the study had already raised it to 120000, sized against the Wave-3 corpus whose largest plan was 70,511 chars). Two Wave-4 plans exceeded the old ceiling: eb6e-f43a-PASS 148,578 and eb6e-f43a-BLOCK 146,643. Behaviourally inert for the other 38 plans (next largest 104,850). (d) Operator direction: rebar's Wave-1 canonical stays as draw 1; no re-runs. Where a cell holds fewer than three, collect the remainder. gstack manifest regeneration was authorised and completed.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: INSTRUMENT CHANGES. (1) runs_gstack.json completed from 19 to all 40 campaign plans by derivation from runs_wave4.json; every derivation rule (code_worktree, verified_at_sha<-code_ref, pinned_plan_source<-plan_doc, pinned_plan_sha256 recomputed) validated against the 19 pre-existing sourced rows before any row was written. desc_chars deliberately omitted as non-derivable; all consumers read it via .get() and no Wave-4 plan carries it in any manifest. (2) Variant-tag dispatch implemented for every arm: rebar w3_batch.sh/w3_rebar_run.py --variant, gstack GSTACK_VARIANT, sp/sp5 SP_VARIANT, ce needed nothing (its --rep already took explicit labels, built for the d1r bridge). _fresh_tag now admits an arm only if it declares runner_variant, so an arm cannot be handed a tag its runner cannot write. (3) extract.py widened to six arms (sp5 added) with a draw axis on every arm, backed by campaign.census rather than reconstructed filenames. (4) ballot.py builds six-arm ballots per draw; legacy four-arm draw-1 shape still rebuilds byte-identically for all 40 plans. (5) New harness/merge_ballot.py produces merged per-plan n=3 ballots. (6) adjudicate.py now verifies the ballot the judges declared, exit 3 on mismatch.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED. (a) Wave-1 manifest gap: w3_rebar_run.load_run and w3_file_impact.derive searched only runs_wave3.json, so wave-1 run ids raised 'unknown run_id' / IndexError before rebar was invoked. Two 2948-48e5-BLOCK draws had been recorded void by it; they were reclassified as instrument failures (nothing ran, nothing billed, nothing written) and both have since been collected. (b) Three grammars narrower than the writer, all now accepting one optional trailing variant letter: campaign.rebar_disk_draws, extract.split_rebar_artifact, and the generic per-arm cost enumeration in independence(). (c) census reconstructed rebar tags as f'rep{n}', discarding the variant letter, so a re-run credited at rep2d was looked up as rep2, matched the original void and left two fully paid verdicts uncredited; it now reads the tag from the filename. (d) adjudicate.py never compared ballot_sha256 -- proven by adjudicating against a deliberately different ballot (exit 0, identical counts, wrong hash stamped). (e) 6120-acda-BLOCK's published adjudication was computed against a ballot none of its three judges read (judges declare 7b743529..., disk holds df08e429...); the ballot they voted on is not on disk. The new gate passes 39 of 40 and refuses exactly that one.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: DEFECTS INTRODUCED BY THIS SESSION AND CORRECTED. (a) The enumerator was widened to hand non-mini arms a fresh tag before the runners could write one; a gstack dispatch for unit .r3b ran as --rep 3 and wrote 7 artifacts to the burned .r3 path. Killed mid-run and archived under wave3/quarantine/killed-variant-dispatch-2026-09-18/ with a README; not deleted, since it was partly paid for. This is the same defect class the original refusal existed to prevent, committed by the change meant to close it. (b) The instrument-failure reclassification was keyed on the unit rather than on the specific historical record, so it swallowed every void at that key including later legitimate ones; affected units read 'claimed' permanently and the reconciler re-voided them each pass, appending 8 spurious void rows before it was noticed. Now pinned to five exact (arm, run, replicate, target, timestamp) records. The spurious rows remain in the append-only ledger. (c) Three separate analyses were reported from misread return shapes before being checked -- independence() returns a 2-tuple of (checks, records); merged-ballot provenance is a dict, not a list. One produced a false '61/61 clean' independence figure; the true figure was unchanged at 50 of 61.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: MEASUREMENTS THAT BEAR ON THE REPORT. (1) Replicability cannot be measured by text matching. Across 8 merged per-plan ballots, 1340 items appear in one draw, 13 in two, 2 in three; all 15 multi-draw items are rebar and all 15 are one of two deterministic banner rows. No arm reproduced a substantive finding's text across runs. Prior work in the study agrees from the other direction: of 618 judge-confirmed same-defect pairs, zero reach jaccard 0.5 and a five-field matcher recovers 44%. Replicability must therefore come from judges linking same-issue rows; merge_ballot records draw_multiplicity_is_a_lower_bound in every artifact so the distribution cannot be quoted as the answer. (2) rebar reads draw 1 from rebar_findings.json (surfaced + overflow + indeterminate) and draws 2-3 from verdict documents (blocking + advisory, i.e. surfaced only). Only rebar uses two readers. Magnitude on complete plans: 2948-48e5-PASS draw 1 holds 27 rows of which 2 were surfaced; 5200-e04e-PASS holds 32 of which 19 were surfaced; on 86ac-086a-PASS and 2127-348c-PASS the populations nearly agree. No row carries a surfaced/suppressed marker. Operator direction is to keep the canonical and carry this as a reporting caveat. (3) Independence: 40 cells report PARTIAL on 'three distinct cost records' across ce, rebar, sp and sp5 -- draw 1 is a frozen earlier-wave canonical with no cost record at the probed path. Only gstack reaches three. mini's 10 step-limit FAILs come from globbing every on-disk artifact including A5-excluded ones; among campaign-tagged mini draws every step limit is 260.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: ARTIFACTS AND OPEN WORK. Written this session: harness/EVIDENCE_RECORD.md (independence per cell, per-arm usage with backend-comparability caveats, itemised rebar invocations that left no artifact); artifacts/ballots/replicates/ 30 six-arm per-draw ballots plus SIX_ARM_INDEX.md; artifacts/ballots/merged/ 8 merged per-plan ballots (ballot_shape merged-draws/v1); harness/merge_ballot.py; harness/fidelity-pending/void-vs-instrument-failure-2948.md; wave3/quarantine/killed-variant-dispatch-2026-09-18/. The canonical non-recursive glob artifacts/ballots/*.ballot.json still returns exactly 40, so neither new shape can be mistaken for a canonical ballot. OPEN: finish collection (404 draws owed); the census reports rebar invocations paid for that left no artifact, now 30 with 26 inside the 40-plan universe and climbing as collection proceeds -- 6120-acda-BLOCK is 4 paid for 0 surviving, and this needs a cause before the report; phase-2 judging has never been run for the n=3 six-arm shape and has no runner script (three independent blind classifier sessions per plan, driven by harness/JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS*.md); harness/fidelity-pending/*.md still needs merging into FIDELITY_LOG.md; final report regeneration against n=3 data. Local-only numbers, including any spend figures, stay out of this log per machine-local policy.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: CONCURRENCY LIMIT, MEASURED THE HARD WAY. Six supervisor lanes were run in parallel at ~23:00Z. 61 voids followed within roughly three hours, against 20 for the whole campaign before that. Two distinct failure modes, both concurrency-induced, neither a defect in the arm under test: mini returned provider InternalServerError with COST 0.0 and CALLS 1 (nothing billed, but the draw is burned); ce exited 8 'INSTRUMENT LOST' with no per-subagent transcript written and the -p background-wait ceiling firing, which its own runner refuses to admit as a draw. gstack and sp5 failed at comparable wall times. The prior working configuration was two lanes. Recommended ceiling: two concurrent lanes, and note that rebar additionally serialises against itself via the shared checkout's plan-review cache guard, so a second rebar dispatch refuses while one is live. Lanes were reduced to zero at the end of this session; two orphaned gstack runners were left to finish and need  afterwards to record their terminal state. The voids from this window are recorded and the affected draws are owed again -- they are not lost, but they consumed wall time and, for the non-mini arms, real spend.
